use_case_name: Monitor Current and Past Auction Status

claims.content: Customer wants to monitor current and past auction status by viewing the current winning bid, countdown clock, item bid history, and the items they have previously bid on (won and not won).

scope_contract.goal_statement: Customer monitors current auction status and past auction history (items previously bid on, with outcomes).
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Customer views the current auction status page showing the current winning bid, countdown clock, and item bid history, and views their past bid list showing items bid on (won and not won); the requested status information is displayed.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Customer decides to check auction status and opens the relevant monitoring view (current auction details or past bid history).
scope_contract.success_boundary: Customer has seen the current winning bid, remaining auction time, item bid history, and their past bid outcomes.
in_scope_actions: View countdown clock showing remaining time until auction closes
View item bid history including bidder member IDs, bid amounts, and bid times
View items the customer previously bid on, including won and not won
excluded_adjacent_actions: Checkout or payment for won items
Managing order history, account status, or contact details
Monitoring expected performance of future auctions for business purposes
variant_dimensions: Type of status monitored: current auction details vs past bid history
Outcome of past bids: won vs not won

claims.content: Customer
The customer is currently bidding on at least one item, so current auction status data is available to display.
The customer has previously bid on at least one item, with a recorded outcome of won or not won, so past bid history data is available to display.

The use case is triggered when the customer decides to monitor current or past auction status and opens the relevant monitoring view: clicking the 'My Current Bid'/'My Current Bids' link in the top navigation/site header or entering the vanity URL www.jtvauctions.com/mybids for current auction details, accessing the 'My Bid History' page for past bid outcomes, or clicking the 'Winner / High Bidder' link in the auction history table.

After the Trigger, the flow branches by the selected entry point: for the My Current Bids view, proceed to step 2, where the system displays the current-bids list; for the My Bid History view, proceed to step 6, where the system displays the won/lost history sections.
Customer opens the My Current Bids page by clicking the 'My Current Bids' link in the site header or entering the vanity URL www.jtvauctions.com/mybids.

System displays the My Current Bids page listing the items the customer is currently bidding on, with columns for Item #, Description, My Current Bid, My SmartBid, Current High Bid, Total Bids, Last Bid Time, Ending Time, and Action.
Customer clicks the Item # link for an item in the My Current Bids list to view its Product Details (Bidding) page.

System displays the Product Details (Bidding) page for that item, showing the current high bid ($65.00), a countdown timer with remaining time (18:57:45), and the item bid history table with bidder names, bid amounts, timestamps, and SmartBid status.
Customer opens the My Bid History page.
System displays the My Bid History page divided into two sections, 'Items I've Won' and 'Items I Bid On, But Did Not Win', with each section sorted by ending time, most recent items on top.

Diverges from Step 3: While the My Current Bids list is displayed, the customer may click any column title to sort the list by that attribute; the system redisplays the list in the selected sort order, and the customer can continue monitoring their current auction status.

Diverges from Step 3: While the system displays the My Current Bids list, if the customer's current bid is less than the Current High Bid, the dollar amount in the 'My Current Bid' column is displayed in bold red; the customer can still continue viewing their current auction status.

Diverges from Step 5: While the Product Details (Bidding) page is displayed with the item bid history table, the customer may click the 'Winner / High Bidder' link in the auction history table; the system displays that bidder's customer history view instead of continuing directly with the standard item details/bid list view.

Diverges from Step 7: In the 'Items I've Won' section of the My Bid History page, if PayPal or Amazon Payments is the customer's default payment type, the Payment Status for a won item may show 'Not Paid' in bold red and link to the 'Returning Winner's Payments' page until the customer has paid for their winnings.

Diverges from main_flow Step 4: If the customer is not signed in when clicking the Item # link (or elsewhere within the product module, except the QuickBid button) to open the Product Details page, the system presents a sign-in page instead of displaying the requested auction status. After the customer completes sign-in, the system delivers the customer to the Product Details page, and the use case resumes at main_flow Step 5.

The system has displayed the Product Details (Bidding) page for the selected current auction item, showing the current high bid, countdown timer with remaining time, and item bid history table with bidder names, bid amounts, timestamps, and SmartBid status.
The system has displayed the My Bid History page with two sections, 'Items I've Won' and 'Items I Bid On, But Did Not Win', showing the customer's past bid outcomes.
The system has displayed the Customer History page for the selected winner/high bidder, showing bid history, order history, account status, and contact details.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] Main Flow step 1 branches only to the My Current Bids view and the My Bid History view, but the Trigger also includes a third entry point: clicking the 'Winner / High Bidder' link in the auction history table. That trigger entry is never picked up by any Main Flow step, which also makes the Customer History page described in Postcondition claim 3 unreachable.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger lists three entry points: My Current Bids/vanity URL, My Bid History, and the Winner / High Bidder link in the auction history table. Main Flow step 1 only continues the current-bids entry; step 5 later reaches My Bid History, but there is no branch/step for a trigger that starts at My Bid History, and no Main Flow claim at all covers the Winner / High Bidder trigger. So a trigger through those routes is not picked up by the Main Flow.

Main Flow step 1 restates the Trigger instead of picking up from it. It says the customer opens the My Current Bids page or the My Bid History page, and then steps 2 and 6 repeat the same opening actions, breaking vertical continuity from Trigger to Main Flow.

Main flow Step 1 includes a trigger via the 'Winner / High Bidder' link that leads to the Customer History page showing bid history, order history, account status, and contact details. The goal is to monitor current and past auction status, and the goal scope explicitly excludes managing order history, account status, and contact details. Thus main_flow contains behavior not aligned with the stated goal.

[slot_rewrite] All alternative flow claims anchor their divergence to a customer action step rather than the main flow step where the referenced page content is displayed: AF1/AF2 diverge from Step 2, but the My Current Bids list is displayed in Step 3; AF3 diverges from Step 4, but the item bid history table is displayed in Step 5; AF4 diverges from Step 6, but the My Bid History page sections are displayed in Step 7. The divergence points therefore do not match the main flow states in which those options exist.

The exception flow diverges from Step 3, but the triggering action 'clicking the Item # link' is main_flow Step 4; after sign-in the system delivers the customer to the Product Details page, which is the result described in main_flow Step 5. The branch therefore resumes at the wrong main_flow step (Step 4 instead of Step 5), so its exit is not consistent with the main flow.

Main Flow step 1 includes a terminal branch via the 'Winner / High Bidder' link in the auction history table that results in the Customer History page being displayed, showing bid history, order history, account status, and contact details. The Postconditions only declare the Product Details (Bidding) page and the My Bid History page, so this branch cannot reach any declared postcondition.
